How to live stream your club's match on Facebook

24 November 2026 · Kadar

For many small clubs the supporters are on Facebook, not on YouTube. The club page is where parents look for the kick-off time, so it is the natural place for the match itself. Streaming there from a phone with a scoreboard takes a stream key and a few minutes of preparation.

1. Check that your page may go live

Facebook sets conditions for live video, such as a minimum age of the account and a minimum number of followers for a page. The conditions change, so open Live Producer a few days before the match and see whether Facebook lets you create a live video. If it does not, it tells you what is missing.

2. Get the stream key

  1. On the club page choose Live video. Facebook opens Live Producer.
  2. Choose Streaming software as the source.
  3. Copy the stream key. Switch on the persistent key, so the same key works for every match and you paste it only once.

The key is a password for your page's live video. Do not post it in a group chat.

3. Paste it into the app and test

In Kadar you open Destinations, switch on Facebook Live and paste the key. Do a two-minute test the evening before, with the audience of the live video set to Only me, and check the picture and the sound on another phone.

4. Make it easy to find

  • Give the live video a title with both clubs and the competition: "FK Loko – FK Sloga, league round 7".
  • Announce the stream on the page the day before and again an hour before kick-off.
  • Ask players and parents to share the post. Facebook shows a live video to more people when it is shared early.
  • Pin the live video to the top of the page while the match is on.

5. During the match

Keep the score in the app, so the scoreboard in the picture is always right. Viewers who join late see the score and the minute at a glance. If a goal is worth a second look, show the replay in the corner window while the live picture continues.

YouTube or Facebook?

Facebook reaches the people who already follow the club. YouTube is easier to search later and keeps a tidy archive of the season. Kadar streams to one destination at a time, so pick the one where your supporters are and post the recording to the other afterwards: the match is saved to the phone either way.

Try it at your next match
